scales.name: Major
scales.applications: Major keys; major and major-7 chords
scales.comparison: Reference scale for all interval formulas.

scales.name: Natural minor
scales.applications: Minor keys; minor and minor-7 chords when the harmony contains b6
scales.comparison: Relative minor of F major; parallel minor of D major.

scales.name: Dorian
scales.applications: Minor-7 grooves, funk, modal jazz, Latin harmony
scales.description: Minor with a brighter, more open sixth
scales.comparison: Natural minor with b6 raised to 6.

scales.name: Phrygian
scales.applications: Minor chords with a strong lowered-second colour; Spanish and metal contexts
scales.description: Dark and compressed around the root
scales.comparison: Natural minor with 2 lowered to b2.

scales.name: Lydian
scales.applications: Major chords with #11; sustained major harmony
scales.description: Bright, floating, less final than Ionian

scales.name: Mixolydian
scales.applications: Dominant-7 chords, blues, funk, rock and salsa harmony
scales.comparison: Major scale with 7 lowered to b7.

scales.name: Locrian
scales.description: Unstable because the perfect fifth is absent

scales.name: Harmonic minor
scales.signature: Raised 7 and the augmented second from b6 to 7
scales.applications: Minor-key cadences; dominant V7 resolving to minor i
scales.comparison: Natural minor with b7 raised to 7.

scales.name: Melodic minor
scales.applications: Minor-major-7 harmony and modern jazz sounds
scales.description: Minor tonic with a smooth upper half
scales.comparison: Diagram uses the ascending/jazz form; classical descent often uses natural minor.

scales.name: Major pentatonic
scales.applications: Major chords, melodic fills, country, soul and pop

scales.name: Minor pentatonic
scales.applications: Minor grooves, blues, rock and funk
scales.comparison: Natural minor with 2 and b6 removed.

scales.name: Blues
scales.applications: Blues language and tension inside minor-pentatonic lines
scales.description: Minor pentatonic with an added chromatic pull

exercises.title: 1-2-3-4 chromatic cell
exercises.instructions: Use fingers 1–2–3–4, then return 4–3–2–1. Repeat on every string.
exercises.target: Equal attacks and minimum left-hand motion.
exercises.progression: Begin at the lower tempo. Add 4 bpm after three clean repetitions; reduce by 6–8 bpm when timing or muting breaks down.

exercises.title: 4-3-2-1 reverse cell
exercises.instructions: Begin with finger 4 and descend. Keep all unused fingers close to the string.
exercises.target: The fourth finger initiates cleanly without collapsing the hand.
exercises.progression: Begin at the lower tempo. Add 4 bpm after three clean repetitions; reduce by 6–8 bpm when timing or muting breaks down.

exercises.title: Permutation 1-3-2-4
exercises.instructions: Use fingering 1–3–2–4, then 4–2–3–1. Move the pattern to each string.
exercises.target: No finger moves before its note is required.
exercises.progression: Begin at the lower tempo. Add 4 bpm after three clean repetitions; reduce by 6–8 bpm when timing or muting breaks down.

exercises.title: Permutation 1-4-2-3
exercises.instructions: Use fingering 1–4–2–3 and reverse. Keep the thumb relaxed behind the neck.
exercises.target: The 1-to-4 reach stays quiet and controlled.
exercises.progression: Begin at the lower tempo. Add 4 bpm after three clean repetitions; reduce by 6–8 bpm when timing or muting breaks down.

exercises.title: Same-fret string ladder
exercises.instructions: Cross all four strings at fret 5 and return. Alternate plucking fingers continuously.
exercises.target: No open-string ringing during either direction change.
exercises.progression: Begin at the lower tempo. Add 4 bpm after three clean repetitions; reduce by 6–8 bpm when timing or muting breaks down.

exercises.title: Diagonal spider outward
exercises.instructions: Assign fingers 1–2–3–4 to the first diagonal, then 1–2–3–4 to the returning diagonal.
exercises.target: Every string change is muted before the next note sounds.
exercises.progression: Begin at the lower tempo. Add 4 bpm after three clean repetitions; reduce by 6–8 bpm when timing or muting breaks down.

exercises.title: Diagonal spider inward
exercises.instructions: Reverse the diagonal direction from P6 while preserving finger assignments.
exercises.target: The hand remains centered; the wrist does not twist between strings.
exercises.progression: Begin at the lower tempo. Add 4 bpm after three clean repetitions; reduce by 6–8 bpm when timing or muting breaks down.

exercises.title: String-skipping ladder
exercises.instructions: Skip one string on every move. Use movable-thumb or floating-thumb muting.
exercises.target: Skipped strings remain completely silent.
exercises.progression: Begin at the lower tempo. Add 4 bpm after three clean repetitions; reduce by 6–8 bpm when timing or muting breaks down.

exercises.title: Two-fret position shift
exercises.instructions: Play frets 5–8, then shift the entire hand to frets 7–10 without pausing.
exercises.target: The shift lands exactly on fret 7 without an audible slide unless deliberately added.
exercises.progression: Begin at the lower tempo. Add 4 bpm after three clean repetitions; reduce by 6–8 bpm when timing or muting breaks down.

exercises.title: Whole-position string shift
exercises.instructions: Ascend across the strings at fret 5, shift to fret 7, and descend.
exercises.target: The left hand shifts as one unit; right-hand alternation does not restart.
exercises.progression: Begin at the lower tempo. Add 4 bpm after three clean repetitions; reduce by 6–8 bpm when timing or muting breaks down.

exercises.title: Movable octave shapes
exercises.instructions: Play each low note followed by its octave two strings higher and two frets forward.
exercises.target: Both notes of every octave pair match in pitch identity and volume.
exercises.progression: Begin at the lower tempo. Add 4 bpm after three clean repetitions; reduce by 6–8 bpm when timing or muting breaks down.

exercises.title: Root-fifth-octave triangle
exercises.instructions: Cycle root–fifth–octave–fifth. Move the shape to G and A after one minute each.
exercises.target: String crossings sound connected without notes overlapping.
exercises.progression: Begin at the lower tempo. Add 4 bpm after three clean repetitions; reduce by 6–8 bpm when timing or muting breaks down.

exercises.title: Minor-third and major-third control
exercises.instructions: Alternate the minor third and major third above D. Use fingers that keep the hand relaxed.
exercises.target: The one-fret distinction is visually, physically and aurally clear.
exercises.progression: Begin at the lower tempo. Add 4 bpm after three clean repetitions; reduce by 6–8 bpm when timing or muting breaks down.

exercises.title: One-fret diagonal crawl
exercises.instructions: Move one fret higher with each higher string, then reverse by one fret per string.
exercises.target: Finger placement stays immediately behind each fret.
exercises.progression: Begin at the lower tempo. Add 4 bpm after three clean repetitions; reduce by 6–8 bpm when timing or muting breaks down.

exercises.title: Three-notes-per-string coordination
exercises.instructions: Use the D-major fingering but treat it as a coordination drill. Reverse after the octave.
exercises.target: String changes do not disturb the eighth-note pulse.
exercises.progression: Begin at the lower tempo. Add 4 bpm after three clean repetitions; reduce by 6–8 bpm when timing or muting breaks down.

exercises.title: Repeated-note plucking alternation
exercises.instructions: Play one D repeatedly with strict index-middle alternation. Start the next repetition with the opposite finger.
exercises.target: No change in tone, volume or timing between plucking fingers.
exercises.progression: Begin at the lower tempo. Add 4 bpm after three clean repetitions; reduce by 6–8 bpm when timing or muting breaks down.

exercises.title: Two-string alternation
exercises.instructions: Alternate A and D strings while maintaining index-middle alternation.
exercises.target: The lower string is muted immediately after each change.
exercises.progression: Begin at the lower tempo. Add 4 bpm after three clean repetitions; reduce by 6–8 bpm when timing or muting breaks down.

exercises.title: Wide string-skip control
exercises.instructions: Alternate between E and G strings. Keep A and D muted throughout.
exercises.target: The attack remains centered despite the two-string leap.
exercises.progression: Begin at the lower tempo. Add 4 bpm after three clean repetitions; reduce by 6–8 bpm when timing or muting breaks down.

exercises.title: Hammer-on and pull-off cell
exercises.instructions: Pluck the first note of each four-note group; use hammer-ons and pull-offs for the remaining notes.
exercises.target: Legato notes match the plucked note in volume and rhythmic placement.
exercises.progression: Begin at the lower tempo. Add 4 bpm after three clean repetitions; reduce by 6–8 bpm when timing or muting breaks down.

exercises.title: Four-string endurance pedal
exercises.instructions: Play four repeated notes on each string without stopping. Reverse the string order on alternate repetitions.
exercises.target: Maintain relaxed hands and consistent sound for the full five minutes.
exercises.progression: Begin at the lower tempo. Add 4 bpm after three clean repetitions; reduce by 6–8 bpm when timing or muting breaks down.

exercises.title: D major scale
exercises.instructions: Play ascending, then reverse. Say either note names or degrees 1–2–3–4–5–6–7–8.
exercises.target: Hear the half steps F-sharp–G and C-sharp–D.
exercises.progression: Begin at the lower tempo. Add 4 bpm after three clean repetitions; reduce by 6–8 bpm when timing or muting breaks down.

exercises.title: D natural minor scale
exercises.instructions: Play ascending and descending. Compare F and B-flat with the major-scale F-sharp and B.
exercises.target: The flat third, flat sixth and flat seventh sound intentional.
exercises.progression: Begin at the lower tempo. Add 4 bpm after three clean repetitions; reduce by 6–8 bpm when timing or muting breaks down.

exercises.title: D major-pentatonic phrase
exercises.instructions: Loop the phrase over a D-major backing track. Change only the rhythm after the notes feel secure.
exercises.target: Every note sounds stable against a D-major chord.
exercises.progression: Begin at the lower tempo. Add 4 bpm after three clean repetitions; reduce by 6–8 bpm when timing or muting breaks down.

exercises.title: D minor-pentatonic phrase
exercises.instructions: Loop over Dm7 or a D-minor groove. End alternate repetitions on F, then D.
exercises.target: The phrase resolves differently on the flat third and root.
exercises.progression: Begin at the lower tempo. Add 4 bpm after three clean repetitions; reduce by 6–8 bpm when timing or muting breaks down.

exercises.title: D blues-scale phrase
exercises.instructions: Treat A-flat as a passing tension between G and A rather than a resting point.
exercises.target: The blue note resolves immediately and does not obscure the chord.
exercises.progression: Begin at the lower tempo. Add 4 bpm after three clean repetitions; reduce by 6–8 bpm when timing or muting breaks down.

exercises.title: D major triad
exercises.instructions: Sing or say 1–3–5–8 while playing. Move the same shape to G and A.
exercises.target: The major third is audible as the defining chord tone.
exercises.progression: Begin at the lower tempo. Add 4 bpm after three clean repetitions; reduce by 6–8 bpm when timing or muting breaks down.

exercises.title: D minor triad
exercises.instructions: Say 1–flat3–5–8. Alternate one repetition of M6 with one repetition of M7.
exercises.target: The ear recognizes the one-fret major/minor change immediately.
exercises.progression: Begin at the lower tempo. Add 4 bpm after three clean repetitions; reduce by 6–8 bpm when timing or muting breaks down.

exercises.title: D dominant-seven arpeggio
exercises.instructions: Play over D7. Emphasize F-sharp and C, the notes that define dominant quality.
exercises.target: The flat seventh sounds like controlled tension, not a wrong major seventh.
exercises.progression: Begin at the lower tempo. Add 4 bpm after three clean repetitions; reduce by 6–8 bpm when timing or muting breaks down.

exercises.title: D minor-seven arpeggio
exercises.instructions: Play over Dm7. Compare directly with M8.
exercises.target: Flat third and flat seventh clearly establish minor-seven harmony.
exercises.progression: Begin at the lower tempo. Add 4 bpm after three clean repetitions; reduce by 6–8 bpm when timing or muting breaks down.

exercises.title: I-IV-V-I root-fifth line
exercises.instructions: Two notes per chord: D–A, G–D, A–E, D–A. Use a D-major I–IV–V–I backing track.
exercises.target: Every chord change is audible from the destination root.
exercises.progression: Begin at the lower tempo. Add 4 bpm after three clean repetitions; reduce by 6–8 bpm when timing or muting breaks down.

exercises.title: I-vi-ii-V root-third targeting
exercises.instructions: Play D–F-sharp, B–D, E–G, A–C-sharp over D–Bm–Em–A.
exercises.target: The third reveals each chord quality while the line remains compact.
exercises.progression: Begin at the lower tempo. Add 4 bpm after three clean repetitions; reduce by 6–8 bpm when timing or muting breaks down.

exercises.title: ii-V-I seventh-chord chain in C
exercises.instructions: Arpeggiate Dm7, G7 and Cmaj7. Listen for F remaining common between Dm7 and G7, then resolving to E over Cmaj7.
exercises.target: Chord tones track the harmony without relying on a single scale.
exercises.progression: Begin at the lower tempo. Add 4 bpm after three clean repetitions; reduce by 6–8 bpm when timing or muting breaks down.

exercises.title: D-major scale in thirds
exercises.instructions: Play adjacent diatonic thirds: 1–3, 2–4, 3–5 and onward.
exercises.target: See the scale as relationships rather than a straight run.
exercises.progression: Begin at the lower tempo. Add 4 bpm after three clean repetitions; reduce by 6–8 bpm when timing or muting breaks down.

exercises.title: Chromatic approaches from below
exercises.instructions: Approach D, G, A and high D from one fret below. Place each target on a strong beat.
exercises.target: The chromatic note points clearly toward the following chord tone.
exercises.progression: Begin at the lower tempo. Add 4 bpm after three clean repetitions; reduce by 6–8 bpm when timing or muting breaks down.

exercises.title: Chromatic approaches from above
exercises.instructions: Approach each target from one fret above. Keep the approach short and the target longer when improvising.
exercises.target: Tension consistently resolves downward by a semitone.
exercises.progression: Begin at the lower tempo. Add 4 bpm after three clean repetitions; reduce by 6–8 bpm when timing or muting breaks down.

exercises.title: Two-sided enclosures
exercises.instructions: Surround each target with one scale step above and one chromatic step below: E–C-sharp–D, A–F-sharp–G, and so on.
exercises.target: The final target sounds metrically stronger than both enclosure notes.
exercises.progression: Begin at the lower tempo. Add 4 bpm after three clean repetitions; reduce by 6–8 bpm when timing or muting breaks down.

exercises.title: D pedal-tone groove
exercises.instructions: Return repeatedly to D while changing the upper note. Accent beats 1 and 3, then move the accents to 2 and 4.
exercises.target: The pedal root anchors the phrase while upper tones create motion.
exercises.progression: Begin at the lower tempo. Add 4 bpm after three clean repetitions; reduce by 6–8 bpm when timing or muting breaks down.

exercises.title: Syncopated D-minor groove
exercises.instructions: Count 1-and-2-and-3-and-4-and. Respect every written rest and let silence shape the line.
exercises.target: Entrances remain accurate after rests; notes do not bleed into silence.
exercises.progression: Begin at the lower tempo. Add 4 bpm after three clean repetitions; reduce by 6–8 bpm when timing or muting breaks down.

exercises.title: Basic Latin two-hit cell
exercises.instructions: Over Dm7 then G7, play the fifth on 2-and and the root on beat 4. Do not add notes on beats 1 or 3.
exercises.target: The offbeat arrives without rushing and beat 4 points into the next measure.
exercises.progression: Begin at the lower tempo. Add 4 bpm after three clean repetitions; reduce by 6–8 bpm when timing or muting breaks down.

exercises.title: Latin ii-V-I-VI turnaround
exercises.instructions: Four bars: Dm7–G7–Cmaj7–A7. In each bar place the fifth on 2-and and the root on beat 4.
exercises.target: The beat-4 root anticipates and propels the next chord while the clave remains undisturbed.
exercises.progression: Begin at the lower tempo. Add 4 bpm after three clean repetitions; reduce by 6–8 bpm when timing or muting breaks down.

blocks.purpose: Use the improvisation workflow on one song
